steps.body: Measure one object with two different units and the counts differ — the bigger the unit, the smaller the count.
steps.narration: Measure one object with two different units and the counts differ — the bigger the unit, the smaller the count.

widget.prompt: Measure this rope with two-unit blocks — four of them cover it.
widget.successFeedback: Four two-unit blocks cover the same rope that took eight one-unit blocks: bigger unit, smaller count.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Every block must be the same size, or the count means nothing.

predict.prompt: Switching to units twice as long, what happens to the count?
predict.reveal: Each unit now covers twice as much, so it takes fewer of them to cover the same object.

options.feedback: A longer unit covers more ground per placement, so the count must go down, not up.

options.label: Exactly the same number
options.feedback: The count only stays the same if the unit stays the same size.

options.label: The object changed length
options.feedback: The object never changed; only the size of the measuring unit did.
